# Sundarī Sutta (Ud 4.8 (PTS Ud 43))

**ID:** Ud 4.8 (PTS Ud 43)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)

**Title (Pali):** Sundarī Sutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ud4.8
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sundarī Sutta* (Ud 4.8, PTS Ud 43) is the eighth discourse of the *Meghiyavagga*, the fourth chapter of the *Udāna*, also numbered sequentially as the thirty-eighth sutta of the collection [Masefield 1997; Pande 1974]. The sutta narrates the plot by wanderers of rival sects (*aññatitthiyā paribbājakā*) who murder the female wanderer Sundarī (*paribbājikā Sundarī*) and hide her body in a moat or trench at Jeta's Grove to falsely incriminate the Buddhist monastic community before King Pasenadi of Kosala [SuttaCentral; Pande 1974; Masefield 1997]. G. C. Pande notes that the narrative prose and the concluding verses in this discourse likely formed an original unit [Pande 1974].

Scholars have discussed the story of Sundarī as an important witness to the development and canonization of narrative and commentarial traditions. Bhikkhu Anālayo points out that the Sundarī murder tale illustrates how commentarial background material gained canonical status in the Theravāda tradition by being incorporated directly into the Pāli *Udāna*; among preserved *Udāna* traditions, this narrative appears only in the Pāli collection and is absent from the Chinese translation of the *Udāna* [Anālayo 2014]. In post-canonical literature, the story is retold in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (to verse 306), which is nearly verbatim identical with the introductory story (*paccuppannavatthu*) to the *Maṇicora Jātaka* (Jātaka 285), both deriving from the *Udāna* narrative [Burlingame 1921]. The incident is also referenced in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.2.5) [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral include passage-level verse parallels in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 306), the *Itivuttaka* (*Āpāyika Sutta*, It 48 / It 2.21), the *Sutta Nipāta* (*Kokālika Sutta*, Snp 3.10), the *Gāndhārī Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 259–273), the *Patna Dharmapada* (P-Dhp 96–120), Sanskrit *Udānavarga* recensions (UV 8 and 32; UVS 8), and Chinese translations (T 210.30, T 212.33, T 213.8, T 213.32) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records substantial Pali-internal text reuse across dozens of texts, most prominently with the *Kosala Saṁyutta* (SN 3, particularly segments matching SN 3.14), the *Sakkāra Sutta* (Ud 2.4), and several sections of the *Vinaya Piṭaka*, including the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Pārājika 2 and 3, Saṅghādisesa 2 and 4) and the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus identifies shared passages with the Sanskrit *Kośāmbakavastu* of the *Vinayavastu* [DharmaNexus].
